faq.question: What does Haruna mean?
faq.answer: Haruna is associated with the Arabic form هَارُون, whose core sense is haruna; aaron (prophet) (hausa form).

faq.question: What is the origin of Haruna?
faq.answer: Haruna is associated with Arabic. Haruna is the Hausa form of Arabic هَارُون (Hārūn), the Quranic form of the prophet Aaron.

faq.question: Is Haruna an Arabic name?
faq.answer: Yes — the underlying form هَارُون is Arabic.

faq.question: Is Haruna an Islamic name?
faq.answer: Haruna can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.question: Is Haruna a Quranic name?
faq.answer: Haruna should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Hārūn is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet Aaron and occurs in the Quran.

faq.answer: In Persian, Haruna is rendered هارون and carries the sense هارون، نام پیامبر.

faq.answer: A romanized syllable approximation is ha-ru-na. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.question: What are the variants of Haruna?
faq.answer: Romanization variants include Haruna, haruna. Script forms are هارون, هَارُون, ہارون, हारून.
